scenes.heading: Measuring and classifying angles
scenes.say: Clock hands, opening doors, a skateboarder's one-eighty. They all turn. Today you'll learn to measure that turn and give every angle its proper name.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A door swings open from the wall
scenes.science: An angle is how far one arm turns from the other
scenes.breaks: a door stops at the wall, but an angle can keep turning past 180° all the way to 360°.
scenes.say: Picture a door swinging open. The angle is how far the door has turned, not how big the door is. Open it straight out from the wall and it has turned ninety degrees. But a door hits the wall, while an angle can keep turning, all the way to three hundred and sixty degrees.
scenes.caption: The angle is how far the door has turned, not how big the door is. Straight out from the wall is 90°. But an angle can keep turning, all the way to 360°.

scenes.heading: Using a protractor
steps: Use the scale that starts at 0
Read where the other arm crosses
scenes.say: To use a protractor, put the centre point on the vertex, where the arms meet. Line up one arm with zero. Use the scale that starts at zero on that arm, and read where the other arm crosses. Then ask: is it smaller or bigger than a right angle?

scenes.heading: Six types of angle
scenes.say: Acute angles are less than ninety degrees. A right angle is exactly ninety. Obtuse is between ninety and one hundred and eighty. Straight is exactly one hundred and eighty. Reflex is between one hundred and eighty and three hundred and sixty. And a full turn of three hundred and sixty degrees is a revolution.
scenes.caption: Acute: less than 90°. Right: exactly 90°. Obtuse: between 90° and 180°. Straight: exactly 180°. Reflex: between 180° and 360°. A full turn of 360° is a revolution.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: Two arms make an obtuse angle of 130°. What is the reflex angle on the other side?
lines: The two angles make a full turn
scenes.say: Two arms make an obtuse angle of one hundred and thirty degrees. What's the reflex angle on the other side? Together they make a full turn, so take three hundred and sixty minus one hundred and thirty. That's two hundred and thirty degrees.
scenes.caption: Two arms make 130°. What's the reflex angle? Together they make a full turn: 360° − 130° = 230°.

scenes.heading: Clock angles
scenes.question: What is the smaller angle between the clock hands at 5 o'clock?
scenes.say: Clocks are full of angles. Three hundred and sixty degrees shared between twelve hour gaps gives thirty degrees per gap. At five o'clock there are five gaps, so five times thirty is one hundred and fifty degrees. That's obtuse.
scenes.caption: 360° shared between 12 hour gaps gives 30° per gap. At 5 o'clock there are 5 gaps: 5 × 30° = 150°. That's obtuse.

points: An angle measures turn, in degrees
Read the protractor scale that starts at 0
scenes.say: Quick recap. An angle measures turn. A full turn is three hundred and sixty degrees. Read the scale that starts at zero. A reflex angle is three hundred and sixty minus the smaller angle. Now try the practice questions!
scenes.caption: Quick recap. An angle measures turn. A full turn is 360°. Read the scale that starts at 0. Reflex = 360° − the smaller angle. Now try the practice questions!
